generation.hypothesis: Concurrent strength-ductility improvement can be achieved in high-entropy alloys through cryo-rolling and annealing, which induces a hierarchical microstructure with fine lamellar regions and coarse non-lamellar regions.
generation.conditions: Room temperature or cryogenic temperature, with a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1
generation.structural_mediator: Hierarchical microstructure with fine lamellar regions and coarse non-lamellar regions
generation.mechanism: The cryo-rolling and annealing process induces a hierarchical microstructure, which enhances the strength and ductility of the alloy through the formation of fine lamellar regions with ultrafine FCC grains and coarse non-lamellar regions with coarse unrecrystallized B2 phase.
generation.predicted_outcome: Yield strength of ~1200 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of ~1500 MPa, with an elongation to failure of ~20%
generation.baseline: As-cast or homogenized high-entropy alloy with a yield strength of ~800 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of ~1000 MPa
generation.boundary: The processing route and alloy composition must be optimized to achieve the desired hierarchical microstructure
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of the hierarchical microstructure formation and its effect on the alloy's properties is not fully understood

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of cryo-rolled and annealed high-entropy alloys with different compositions and processing routes
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength do not increase with the formation of a hierarchical microstructure, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Paper card. Question: How can cryo-rolling and annealing be utilized to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in multiphase high entropy alloys, specifically regarding the development of a hierarchical microstructure?. System: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (EHEA). Processing: Multi-pass cryo-rolling up to ~90% reduction in thickness with immersion in liquid N2 for 45 minutes before and after each pass, followed by annealing at 800 °C for 1 hour and water quenching.. Test conditions: Tensile tests at ambient temperature with an initial strain rate of 8.3 × 10−4 s−1; Nano-indentation with load increased linearly from 1 μN to 500 μN over 0.25 seconds.. Findings: The cryo-rolled and annealed material achieved a Yield Strength (YS) of 1437 ± 26 MPa and Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS) of 1562 ± 33 MPa.; The elongation to failure (ef) was approximately 14 ± 1%, which remained almost unchanged compared to the as-cast mat

Question: How can severe cryo-rolling followed by annealing be used to tailor heterogeneous microstructures and overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in brittle intermetallic-containing high entropy alloys?. System: CoCrFeNi2.1Nb0.2 high entropy alloy (FCC matrix with complex Laves phase particles). Processing: Homogenized ingots (1200 °C/24 h) were multi-pass cold- or cryo-rolled to 90% reduction in thickness (final thickness ~0.4 mm); cryo-rolling involved immersion in liquid N2 for 0.5 h before and after every pass; subsequent annealing at 800 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching.. Test conditions: Tensile tests conducted at ambient temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1 using dog-bone shaped specimens..
